title: Existence and uniqueness of the trace of a finite etale morphism
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For an object $w:W\to X$ of the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] write $W_Y=W\times_XY$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projection $p_W:W_Y\to W$; $W_Y$ with $w\circ p_W$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$, and with its projection to $Y$ an object of $Y_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and an etale $j:V\to X$ let $\rho^j_F:j^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_V$ be the isomorphism, natural in $F$, of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] ($F|_V(V'\to V)=F(V'\to V\to X)$). Since $(f_*f^{-1}F)(W)=(f^{-1}F)(W_Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $c_{F,W}=\rho^f_F(W_Y):(f_*f^{-1}F)(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(W_Y)$. For a morphism $\operatorname{tr}:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ write $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_W=\operatorname{tr}(W)\circ c_{F,W}^{-1}:F(W_Y)\to F(W)$.

Then there is a family of morphisms of abelian sheaves $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$, indexed by all finite etale morphisms $f:Y\to X$ (all schemes $X$) and all $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, and it is the unique family with the following properties:

(0) *naturality in $F$*: for every morphism $\varphi:F\to G$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, $\varphi\circ\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=\operatorname{tr}_{f,G}\circ f_*f^{-1}\varphi$;

(1) *compatibility with etale localization on $X$*: let $g:X'\to X$ be etale, $Y'=Y\times_XX'$ and $f':Y'\to X'$ the projection (finite etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]). For an object $W\to X'$ of $X'_{\Et}$, regarded as the object $W\to X'\xrightarrow{g}X$ of $X_{\Et}$, let $\kappa_W:W\times_{X'}Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}W\times_XY$ be the canonical isomorphism over $W$ (pasting of cartesian squares [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]). Then for every such $W$
$$\rho^g_F(W)\circ\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f',g^{-1}F,W}=\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}\circ F(\kappa_W)^{-1}\circ\rho^g_F(W\times_{X'}Y'):(g^{-1}F)(W\times_{X'}Y')\to F(W)$$
(this is the componentwise form of $g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=\operatorname{tr}_{f',g^{-1}F}$ under the canonical identification $g^{-1}f_*f^{-1}F\cong f'_*f'^{-1}g^{-1}F$, both sides of which have $F(W\times_XY)$ as sections over $W$);

(2) *the split case*: suppose $Y=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ for a finite set $J$ (possibly empty) and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j$ covering $Y$, such that each $f|_{V_j}:V_j\to X$ is an isomorphism; let $s_j:X\to Y$ be its inverse followed by the inclusion. For an object $w:W\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ let $\sigma_{j,W}=(\mathrm{id}_W,s_j\circ w):W\to W_Y$ (a morphism of $X_{\Et}$). Then for every $W$ and every $t\in F(W_Y)$,
$$\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}(t)=\sum_{j\in J}F(\sigma_{j,W})(t).$$
In particular, for $Y=\coprod_{i=1}^dX$ ($d\ge0$, the coproduct of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-copies]) and $f$ the identity on each summand, take $V_i$ the image of the $i$-th coprojection: under $(f_*f^{-1}F)(W)\cong F(W)^d$, $t\mapsto(F(\sigma_{i,W})c_{F,W}(t))_i$ (an isomorphism by the sheaf condition; this reformulation is not part of the assertion), $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$ is the sum map $F^{\oplus d}\to F$.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'; uses Etale Morphisms Lemma 04HN (etale.tex, lemma-finite-etale-etale-local)

proof.text: *Reduction to presheaf maps $F(W_Y)\to F(W)$.* For $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ let $P_F$ be the presheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\Et}$ with $P_F(W)=F(W_Y)$ and, for a morphism $h:W'\to W$ of $X_{\Et}$, restriction $F(h_Y)$, where $h_Y=h\times_X\mathrm{id}_Y:W'_Y\to W_Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; $h_Y$ is a morphism over $X$ between objects of $X_{\Et}$ ($W_Y\to X$ is etale as the composite of the base change $p_W$ of the etale $f$ with $w$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits(1), lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(2)]), and $(h\circ h')_Y=h_Y\circ h'_Y$, $(\mathrm{id}_W)_Y=\mathrm{id}$ by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. By the definition of direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $P_F$ is literally $f_*(F|_Y)$ ($F|_Y(W_Y\to Y)=F(W_Y\to Y\to X)$, and $W_Y\to Y\to X$ equals $w\circ p_W$), so $P_F$ is an abelian sheaf, and $c_F=f_*(\rho^f_F):f_*f^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F$, with components $c_{F,W}$, is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves natural in $F$, since $\rho^f$ is natural in $F$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction(1)] ($f$ is etale) and $f_*$ is a functor. Hence giving a morphism $\operatorname{tr}:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ is the same as giving a morphism of presheaves $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}=\operatorname{tr}\circ c_F^{-1}:P_F\to F$, i.e. maps $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_W:F(W_Y)\to F(W)$ that are additive and satisfy $F(h)\circ\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_W=\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{W'}\circ F(h_Y)$ for all $h:W'\to W$ ($\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is a full subcategory of presheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]); and $\operatorname{tr}$ is natural in $F$ in the sense of (0) iff $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}$ is, i.e. $\varphi_W\circ\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}=\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,G,W}\circ\varphi_{W_Y}$ for $\varphi:F\to G$ (because $c_G\circ f_*f^{-1}\varphi=f_*(\varphi|_Y)\circ c_F$ and $f_*(\varphi|_Y)$ has components $\varphi_{W_Y}$). The base change $f'$ in (1) is finite etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence(a)] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits(1)], so (1) makes sense; and $\kappa_W$ is an isomorphism over $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] (the squares $W\times_{X'}Y'\to Y'\to Y$ over $W\to X'\to X$), hence an isomorphism of $X_{\Et}$.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'

proof.text: *Splittings and local sums.* For an object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$, a *splitting* $D$ of $T_Y$ is a finite set $J$ and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j\subseteq T_Y$ ($j\in J$) covering $T_Y$ such that each $p_T|_{V_j}:V_j\to T$ is an isomorphism; its *sections* are $\sigma_j:T\to T_Y$, the inverse of $p_T|_{V_j}$ followed by the inclusion, so $p_T\circ\sigma_j=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $\sigma_j$ is a morphism over $T$, hence over $X$, i.e. a morphism of $X_{\Et}$. For $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ the *local sum* is $\Sigma_D:F(T_Y)\to F(T)$, $\Sigma_D(t)=\sum_{j\in J}F(\sigma_j)(t)$ (zero if $J=\varnothing$). It is additive (each $F(\sigma_j)$ is a homomorphism) and natural in $F$: for $\varphi:F\to G$, $\varphi_T\circ\Sigma^F_D=\Sigma^G_D\circ\varphi_{T_Y}$, since $\varphi_T\circ F(\sigma_j)=G(\sigma_j)\circ\varphi_{T_Y}$ ($\varphi$ is a natural transformation [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]) and $\varphi_T$ is additive. In this notation property (2) says: if $Y$ is split by $(V_j)$ with sections $s_j$, then $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}=\Sigma_{D_W}$ where $D_W$ is the splitting of $W_Y$ with sections $\sigma_{j,W}$ (that $D_W$ is a splitting is step 3 applied to $w:W\to X$, see step 8).

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'

proof.text:
*Pulling back a splitting.* Let $D=(V_j,\sigma_j)_{j\in J}$ be a splitting of $T_Y$ and $h:T'\to T$ a morphism of $X_{\Et}$. In the diagram $T'_Y\xrightarrow{h_Y}T_Y\to Y$ over $T'\xrightarrow{h}T\to X$ the right square and the outer rectangle are cartesian, so the left square is cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]: $T'_Y=T'\times_TT_Y$ with projections $p_{T'}$ and $h_Y$. Put $V'_j=h_Y^{-1}(V_j)$: these are pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $T'_Y$ (preimages of such), and $V'_j=T'\times_TV_j$ as open subscheme of $T'\times_TT_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], with $p_{T'}|_{V'_j}$ the base change of the isomorphism $p_T|_{V_j}$ along $h$, hence an isomorphism (the base change of an isomorphism is one, by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]). Let $\sigma'_j:T'\to T'_Y$ be the unique morphism with $p_{T'}\circ\sigma'_j=\mathrm{id}_{T'}$ and $h_Y\circ\sigma'_j=\sigma_j\circ h$ (it exists since $p_T\circ\sigma_j\circ h=h$); as $h_Y\sigma'_j$ lands in $V_j$, $\sigma'_j$ lands in $V'_j$, so it is the inverse of the isomorphism $p_{T'}|_{V'_j}$ followed by the inclusion. Thus $h^*D=(V'_j,\sigma'_j)_{j\in J}$ is a splitting of $T'_Y$, and for $t\in F(T_Y)$
$$F(h)(\Sigma_D(t))=\sum_jF(\sigma_j\circ h)(t)=\sum_jF(h_Y\circ\sigma'_j)(t)=\Sigma_{h^*D}(F(h_Y)(t)),$$
using that $F$ is a functor to abelian groups. Also $(h\circ h'')^*D$ and $h''^*h^*D$ have the same pieces.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'

proof.text:
*The local sum does not depend on the splitting.* Let $D=(V_j,\sigma_j)_{j\in J}$ and $E=(V'_k,\sigma'_k)_{k\in K}$ be two splittings of the same $T_Y$ and $t\in F(T_Y)$; we show $\Sigma_D(t)=\Sigma_E(t)$. (This is the point the earlier attempt left unargued; Stacks and SGA 4 leave it to 'the usual descent argument'.) For $j\in J,k\in K$ the set $V_j\cap V'_k$ is open and closed in $V_j$, and $p_T|_{V_j}$ is an isomorphism, so $T_{jk}=p_T(V_j\cap V'_k)$ is an open (and closed) subset of $T$, and $p_T$ restricts to an isomorphism of the open subschemes $V_j\cap V'_k\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{jk}$. (a) For fixed $j$ the $T_{jk}$, $k\in K$, are pairwise disjoint and cover $T$ (the $V_j\cap V'_k$ partition $V_j$ and $p_T|_{V_j}$ is bijective onto $T$); for fixed $k$ the $T_{jk}$, $j\in J$, are pairwise disjoint and cover $T$ (same argument with $V'_k$). (b) $\sigma_j|_{T_{jk}}=\sigma'_k|_{T_{jk}}$: since $\sigma_j$ is inverse to $p_T|_{V_j}$, $\sigma_j(T_{jk})=V_j\cap V'_k$, and likewise $\sigma'_k(T_{jk})=V_j\cap V'_k$; so both restrictions factor through the open subscheme $V_j\cap V'_k$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and both are right inverses of the isomorphism $p_T:V_j\cap V'_k\to T_{jk}$ (as $p_T\sigma_j=p_T\sigma'_k=\mathrm{id}_T$), hence both equal its inverse. (c) For a point $x\in T$ let $\pi_x(j)$ be the unique $k$ with $x\in T_{jk}$ (by (a)); $\pi_x:J\to K$ is injective (if $\pi_x(j)=\pi_x(j')=k$ then $x\in T_{jk}\cap T_{j'k}$, so $j=j'$ by (a)) and surjective ($x$ lies in some $T_{jk}$ for each $k$ by (a)), so it is a bijection. For each bijection $\pi:J\to K$ let $T_\pi=\bigcap_{j\in J}T_{j\pi(j)}$, an open subscheme of $T$ with inclusion $\iota_\pi$; then $x\in T_{\pi_x}$, so the finitely many $\iota_\pi$ are jointly surjective open immersions, which are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(1)]; so $T_\pi\to T\to X$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$ (ibid. (2)) and $\{\iota_\pi:T_\pi\to T\}_\pi$ is a covering of $T$ in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (the empty family if $T=\varnothing$, which covers $\varnothing$). (d) By (b), $\sigma_j\circ\iota_\pi=\sigma'_{\pi(j)}\circ\iota_\pi$ for all $j$, so, reindexing the sum by the bijection $\pi$,
$$F(\iota_\pi)(\Sigma_D(t))=\sum_{j\in J}F(\sigma_j\iota_\pi)(t)=\sum_{j\in J}F(\sigma'_{\pi(j)}\iota_\pi)(t)=\sum_{k\in K}F(\sigma'_k\iota_\pi)(t)=F(\iota_\pi)(\Sigma_E(t)).$$
Since $F$ is a sheaf, $F(T)\to\prod_\pi F(T_\pi)$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], so $\Sigma_D(t)=\Sigma_E(t)$. (If $|J|\ne|K|$ there is no $\pi$, $T=\varnothing$ and $F(T)=0$.)

proof.text: *Splitting coverings exist.* Let $T$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$. For each $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] (Stacks 04HN) gives an etale $g_x:U_x\to X$, a point $u_x\in U_x$ over $x$, and a decomposition of $Y\times_XU_x$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes each mapped isomorphically onto $U_x$ by the second projection; transporting it along the canonical isomorphism $Y\times_XU_x\cong U_x\times_XY=(U_x)_Y$ over $U_x$ [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a splitting $D_x$ of $(U_x)_Y$ (with $U_x$ an object of $X_{\Et}$ via $g_x$). The family $(g_x)_{x\in X}$ is etale and jointly surjective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] the projections $q_x:T_x=T\times_XU_x\to T$ are etale and jointly surjective; $T_x$ with $T_x\to T\to X$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(2)], $\{q_x\}_x$ is a covering of $T$ in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and the second projection $r_x:T_x\to U_x$ is a morphism of $X_{\Et}$, so $r_x^*D_x$ is a splitting of $(T_x)_Y$ by step 3. So every object of $X_{\Et}$ has a covering in $X_{\Et}$ by objects $T_a$ with $(T_a)_Y$ split. This is where finiteness of $f$ enters; it is the statement 'every finite etale morphism is etale locally on $X$ of the form (2)' of Stacks 03SH / 'tout revetement etale est localement constant' of SGA 4 IX 5.1.

proof.text:
*Construction of $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_W$ by descent.* Fix $F$, an object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ and $t\in F(W_Y)$. Claim: there is exactly one $u\in F(W)$ such that
(*) for every morphism $h:T\to W$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every splitting $D$ of $T_Y$, $F(h)(u)=\Sigma_D(F(h_Y)(t))$.
*Uniqueness:* take a covering $\{h_a:W_a\to W\}$ with splittings $D_a$ of $(W_a)_Y$ (step 5); two such $u$ have the same image in every $F(W_a)$, hence are equal since $F$ is separated [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. *Existence:* with this covering put $u_a=\Sigma_{D_a}(F((h_a)_Y)(t))\in F(W_a)$. For indices $a,b$ let $W_{ab}=W_a\times_WW_b$ (an object of $X_{\Et}$, the fibre product in $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits(2)]) with projections $\mathrm{pr}_a,\mathrm{pr}_b$, and $e=h_a\mathrm{pr}_a=h_b\mathrm{pr}_b$. By step 3, $F(\mathrm{pr}_a)(u_a)=\Sigma_{\mathrm{pr}_a^*D_a}(F((\mathrm{pr}_a)_Y)F((h_a)_Y)(t))=\Sigma_{\mathrm{pr}_a^*D_a}(F(e_Y)(t))$ and likewise $F(\mathrm{pr}_b)(u_b)=\Sigma_{\mathrm{pr}_b^*D_b}(F(e_Y)(t))$: two local sums of the same element over two splittings of $(W_{ab})_Y$, equal by step 4. By the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] there is $u\in F(W)$ with $F(h_a)(u)=u_a$ for all $a$. *$u$ satisfies (*):* let $h:T\to W$ and $D$ be given; the projections $q_a:T_a=T\times_WW_a\to T$ form a covering of $T$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with second projections $r_a:T_a\to W_a$, $hq_a=h_ar_a$. Then $F(q_a)F(h)(u)=F(r_a)(u_a)=\Sigma_{r_a^*D_a}(F((h_ar_a)_Y)(t))$ and $F(q_a)(\Sigma_D(F(h_Y)(t)))=\Sigma_{q_a^*D}(F((hq_a)_Y)(t))$ (step 3 twice); these are local sums of one element over two splittings of $(T_a)_Y$, equal by step 4. So $F(h)(u)$ and $\Sigma_D(F(h_Y)(t))$ agree on a covering of $T$ and are equal. Define $\tau_{f,F,W}(t)=u$.

source.place: SGA 4 Expose IX, 5.1: 'Le morphisme trace est caracterise par les deux proprietes suivantes ... L'unicite est triviale a partir de (i), (ii) puisque tout revetement etale est localement constant. Ayant l'unicite, l'existence s'ensuit par l'argument usuel de descente.'

proof.text: *$\tau$ is a morphism of sheaves, natural in $F$; definition of the trace and (0).* All three facts follow from the uniqueness in (*) (step 6). Additivity: if $u,u'$ satisfy (*) for $t,t'$, then $u+u'$ satisfies (*) for $t+t'$ ($F(h)$, $F(h_Y)$ and $\Sigma_D$ are additive, step 2), so $\tau_W(t+t')=\tau_W(t)+\tau_W(t')$. Compatibility with restriction: for $k:W'\to W$ in $X_{\Et}$, the element $F(k)(\tau_W(t))$ satisfies (*) for $(W',F(k_Y)(t))$: for $h:T\to W'$ and a splitting $D$ of $T_Y$, $F(h)F(k)(\tau_W(t))=F(kh)(\tau_W(t))=\Sigma_D(F((kh)_Y)(t))=\Sigma_D(F(h_Y)F(k_Y)(t))$ (step 1: $(kh)_Y=k_Yh_Y$); so $F(k)\circ\tau_W=\tau_{W'}\circ F(k_Y)$, i.e. $\tau_{f,F}:P_F\to F$ is a morphism of presheaves, hence of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Naturality in $F$: for $\varphi:F\to G$, $\varphi_W(\tau^F_W(t))$ satisfies (*) for $G$ and $\varphi_{W_Y}(t)$: $G(h)\varphi_W(\tau^F_W(t))=\varphi_T(F(h)\tau^F_W(t))=\varphi_T(\Sigma_D(F(h_Y)t))=\Sigma_D(G(h_Y)\varphi_{W_Y}(t))$ (naturality of $\varphi$ and of $\Sigma_D$, step 2); so $\varphi_W\circ\tau^F_W=\tau^G_W\circ\varphi_{W_Y}$. Define $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=\tau_{f,F}\circ c_F:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$, so $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F}=\tau_{f,F}$; by step 1 it is a morphism of abelian sheaves and satisfies (0).

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'

proof.text: *Property (2).* Suppose $Y=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ as in (2), with sections $s_j:X\to Y$. Regard $X$ (with $\mathrm{id}_X$) as an object of $X_{\Et}$; under the canonical isomorphism $X_Y=X\times_XY\cong Y$ over $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] the $V_j$ give a splitting $D_X$ of $X_Y$ with sections $(\mathrm{id}_X,s_j)$. For an object $w:W\to X$, step 3 applied to the morphism $w:W\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ gives the splitting $w^*D_X$ of $W_Y$, whose sections $\sigma'_j$ are characterized by $p_W\sigma'_j=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $w_Y\sigma'_j=(\mathrm{id}_X,s_j)\circ w$, i.e. (composing with the projection to $Y$) $\sigma'_j=(\mathrm{id}_W,s_j\circ w)=\sigma_{j,W}$. Applying (*) of step 6 with $h=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $D=w^*D_X$: $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}(t)=\tau_W(t)=\sum_jF(\sigma_{j,W})(t)$, which is (2). For $Y=\coprod_{i=1}^dX$ the images $V_i$ of the coprojections are open (and closed, their complement being the union of the others), pairwise disjoint and cover $Y$, and each coprojection is an open immersion inverse to $f|_{V_i}$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-copies], so this case is included with $s_i$ the coprojections.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'

proof.text:
*Property (1).* Let $g:X'\to X$, $f':Y'\to X'$ be as in (1); $Y'$ is finite etale over $X'$ (step 1), so steps 2-7 apply to $f'$. First take the abelian sheaf $F|_{X'}$ on $X'_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction(1)]. For an object $W$ of $X'_{\Et}$ and $t'\in F|_{X'}(W\times_{X'}Y')=F(W\times_{X'}Y')$ put $u=\tau_{f,F,W}(F(\kappa_W)^{-1}t')$; we check that $u$ satisfies (*) of step 6 for $(f',F|_{X'},W,t')$. Let $h:T\to W$ be a morphism of $X'_{\Et}$ (also one of $X_{\Et}$) and $D'=(V'_j,\sigma'_j)$ a splitting of $T\times_{X'}Y'$ over $T$. Since $\kappa_T$ is an isomorphism over $T$, $D=(\kappa_T(V'_j),\kappa_T\sigma'_j)$ is a splitting of $T_Y$. The two morphisms $h_Y\kappa_T$ and $\kappa_Wh_{Y'}$ from $T\times_{X'}Y'$ to $W_Y$ agree after composing with both projections to $W$ and to $Y$, hence are equal [def-pc-fibre-product]. So, using (*) for $u$ (step 6, for $f$),
$$F(h)(u)=\Sigma_D(F(h_Y)F(\kappa_W)^{-1}t')=\sum_jF(\sigma'_j)F(\kappa_T)F(h_Y)F(\kappa_W)^{-1}t'=\sum_jF(\sigma'_j)F(h_{Y'})t'=\Sigma_{D'}(F|_{X'}(h_{Y'})t'),$$
since $F(\kappa_T)F(h_Y)=F(h_Y\kappa_T)=F(\kappa_Wh_{Y'})=F(h_{Y'})F(\kappa_W)$. By uniqueness in (*) for $f'$, $\tau_{f',F|_{X'},W}=\tau_{f,F,W}\circ F(\kappa_W)^{-1}$. Now $\rho^g_F:g^{-1}F\to F|_{X'}$ is a morphism of abelian sheaves on $X'_{\Et}$, so naturality of $\tau_{f'}$ in the sheaf (step 7) gives $\rho^g_F(W)\circ\tau_{f',g^{-1}F,W}=\tau_{f',F|_{X'},W}\circ\rho^g_F(W\times_{X'}Y')=\tau_{f,F,W}\circ F(\kappa_W)^{-1}\circ\rho^g_F(W\times_{X'}Y')$. As $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}=\tau$ (step 7), this is (1). (The parenthetical reformulation in (1) is the componentwise reading through $\rho^g$, which by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction(1)] turns $g^{-1}$ of a morphism $\psi$ into the family of its components $\psi_W$ at the objects $W\to X'\to X$.)

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'

proof.text:
*Uniqueness.* Let $(\operatorname{t}_{f,F})$ be any family of morphisms $f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ with properties (1) and (2) ((0) is not needed). Fix $f,F$; $\overline{\operatorname{t}}=\operatorname{t}_{f,F}\circ c_F^{-1}:P_F\to F$ is a morphism of presheaves (step 1). We show that for every $W$ and $t\in F(W_Y)$ the element $\overline{\operatorname{t}}_W(t)$ satisfies (*) of step 6; then $\overline{\operatorname{t}}_W=\tau_{f,F,W}$ by the uniqueness there, so $\operatorname{t}_{f,F}=\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$. Let $h:T\to W$ and a splitting $D=(V_j,\sigma_j)_{j\in J}$ of $T_Y$ be given. As $\overline{\operatorname{t}}$ is a presheaf map, $F(h)(\overline{\operatorname{t}}_W(t))=\overline{\operatorname{t}}_T(F(h_Y)t)$, so it suffices to show $\overline{\operatorname{t}}_{f,F,T}=\Sigma_D$. Apply (1) to the etale structure morphism $g:T\to X$ ($X'=T$, $Y'=Y\times_XT$, $f':Y'\to T$) and the object $W'=T$ (with $\mathrm{id}_T$) of $T_{\Et}$, whose image in $X_{\Et}$ is $T$: with $\kappa=\kappa_{T}:T\times_TY'\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Y$ (an isomorphism over $T$), and $G=g^{-1}F$,
$$\rho^g_F(T)\circ\overline{\operatorname{t}}_{f',G,T}=\overline{\operatorname{t}}_{f,F,T}\circ F(\kappa)^{-1}\circ\rho^g_F(T\times_TY').$$
The pieces $\kappa^{-1}(V_j)$ split $T\times_TY'$; transported along the isomorphism $T\times_TY'\cong Y'$ over $T$ they show that $Y'$ is as in (2) over $X'=T$, and for the object $\mathrm{id}_T$ the morphisms $\sigma_{j,T}$ of (2) are $\kappa^{-1}\sigma_j$ (both are sections over $T$ landing in $\kappa^{-1}(V_j)$, hence the inverse of the isomorphism $\kappa^{-1}(V_j)\to T$). So by (2) $\overline{\operatorname{t}}_{f',G,T}=\sum_jG(\kappa^{-1}\sigma_j)$, and by naturality of $\rho^g_F$ as a morphism $G\to F|_T$ of sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction(1)], $\rho^g_F(T)\circ G(\kappa^{-1}\sigma_j)=F(\kappa^{-1}\sigma_j)\circ\rho^g_F(T\times_TY')$. Since $\rho^g_F(T\times_TY')$ is bijective, $\overline{\operatorname{t}}_{f,F,T}\circ F(\kappa)^{-1}=\sum_jF(\kappa^{-1}\sigma_j)=\sum_jF(\sigma_j)\circ F(\kappa^{-1})$, and $F(\kappa^{-1})=F(\kappa)^{-1}$, so $\overline{\operatorname{t}}_{f,F,T}=\sum_jF(\sigma_j)=\Sigma_D$. Hence the family of step 7 is the only one with (0), (1), (2). This is SGA 4 IX 5.1 'l'unicite est triviale a partir de (i), (ii) puisque tout revetement etale est localement constant': the local constancy enters through step 6, whose uniqueness rests on the coverings of step 5.
